topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecturer, the scope of the cancer lecture series, and the specific learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, risk factors, and epidemiological variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the interplay between intrinsic genetic errors, environmental exposures, and population-level epidemiological patterns in cancer causation.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious pathogens drive cancer development, focusing on the mechanism of Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms through which physical and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic tumor promotion and developmental susceptibilities that cooperate with initial mutations to drive tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and evaluating exposure risks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to determine carcinogenicity and evaluate exposure risks.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the closing summary of key lecture concepts and final concluding remarks.
